title: Privacy & Product Counsel
posting_excerpt:
WHO THRIVES IN THIS ROLE

The right person in this role is quick to turn regulatory nuance into a product decision and show up with both engineers and enterprise counterparts.

The profile:

 - You have 6–7 years of PQE in privacy and product/commercial counsel, ideally split between in-house work at a data-intensive or AI company and enterprise contract negotiation.

 - You're genuinely fluent across US, UK, and EU privacy law — CCPA/CPRA and the state patchwork, UK GDPR/DPA 2018, and EU GDPR.

 - You think like a product person, not just a lawyer. You'd rather sit in a design review and shape a data flow before it's built than redline it after.

 - You've negotiated enterprise DPAs, security addenda, and cross-border transfer mechanisms directly.

 - You're a genuine generalist, not just a specialist who's willing to help out.

 - You communicate with clarity and conviction. You can explain a data-retention tradeoff to a founder, hold your ground with an enterprise customer's outside counsel, and walk an engineer through why a feature needs a consent gate — all in the same day.

 - You take ownership. There's no one to hand this to. If the privacy program has a gap, you close it. If a deal is stuck on a legal term, you find the path through.

 - You move at startup speed. Deals close fast, product ships fast, and you're available and responsive without needing a legal-ops process to get there.
   
   

Location

San Francisco or London, hybrid, with occasional travel for customer engagements and to work with the other office.
